|strategy=Light side: If you control, force drain +1

Dark side: If you control, [[Kessel Run]] is canceled.

The lightside version of [[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]] can cause a change of plans by the Imperial player if they were ignoring your space armada. A force drain of three per turn is pretty dramatic.

This card can be difficult to play effectively. If played early it can provide the dark player with much needed force, which is a definite negative. NEVER give your opponent what they need. They just might be waiting to deploy the [[Devastator]] and a handful of ties. On the other hand, if you wait too long to play this location, you don't reap the rewards of the force drain. Sometimes, the best strategy could be to wait for the imperial to either play or lose their copy of [[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]] (which is pretty common in most dark decks), and then play your own.

[[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]] can also be used to effectively draw the opponent into a battle, especially if you're waiting to spring a trap using wonderful cards such as full throttle, out of nowhere, etc etc.

The light version of [[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]] is one of the reasons so many Dark players play with their version. But when they beleive you don't have it in your hand they will play their version, which is the time to put down yours. The -1 deploy of the dark version of [[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]] for their Tie's is nice to get rid of.

Also [[Kessel Run]] is a fun, even if it's not the best, way to retreive lost force. And you can't be SURE that your opponent will be playing with [[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]].

Negative side: Giving force to your opponent is always bad, the more they draw, the more they can put down. Also the fact that it only gives the light player one force per turn, and it doesn't give the battle advantages which [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] and [[Yavin 4 (Dark){{!}}Yavin 4]] give.

Best Combo: [[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]], [[Corellian Corvette]], [[Corellian Corvette]], [[Corellian Corvette]]. You NEED to defend this location, or it loses it's effectiveness.<ref name="decipher-strategy">https://web.archive.org/web/20020803215451/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/light/small/kessel.html</ref>
|rulings=* (Light side text) Passengers do not count toward the 6 ability requirement. If the requirement is not met, Light does not get any battle destiny draws (even if they have multiple battle destiny adders such as [[Captain Han Solo]], [[Life Debt]], etc). However, 'draws if unable to otherwise' still works without 6 ability.<ref name="scomp">Players Committee [[Media:SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf|Advanced Rulebook (2023)]], PDF page 59, battle-destiny conditions and the “if unable” exception; PDF page 90, passengers do not apply ability toward battle destiny. This concerns the Light-side ability condition, which is unchanged on these faces, not the different Dark-side Tarkin wording.</ref>

* Only the Dark-side paragraph is supplied by this document entry. The Light-side clause displayed above — “Total ability of 6 or more required for you to draw battle destiny here” — is inherited from the actual printed Dark-side Kessel card, not quoted from the supplement.<ref name="physical-light-clause">[[:File:Premiere-D-kessel-hires.webp|Actual physical Premiere Limited Dark Kessel scan]], Light-side bar; credited scan by strangewayes.</ref> The same physical source supplies parsec 8 and both sets of Force/planet icons.
* The document does not print a destiny number. Destiny 0 is a rule-derived Location value, stated in both the original Glossary and current Advanced Rulebook; it is not a number copied from the image.<ref name="location-rule-defaults">[[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary (1998)]], PDF page 84, Locations; [[Media:SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf|Advanced Rulebook (2023)]], PDF pages 83–84, Locations.</ref>
* Locations have no deploy cost and deploy for free under those same rules. This is recorded here in prose rather than inventing a printed deploy-cost box. The documentary entry prints no D-E1 mark.
* The credited [[:File:Premiere-D-kessel-errata-hires.webp|strangewayes print-ready full-card fan rendition]] uses matching replacement words and a gold E mark. It is retained as an explicit fan comparison, not an automatic high-resolution scan of the actual historical PDF entry. The file, original TIFF provenance and credit are preserved.
* Later official PC image publications remain documented separately at [[Kessel (Dark) (PC Errata)]], [[Kessel (Dark) (PC Errata 2)]], [[Kessel (Dark) (PC Errata 3)]], [[Kessel (Dark) (PC Errata 4)]] and [[Kessel (Dark) (PC Errata 5)]].
